summary.summary_text: PGP Glass Ceylon manufactures glass containers (bottles/jars) for beverage, cosmetics/perfumery, and pharmaceutical customers in Sri Lanka, selling domestically and via export, with the US a growing export destination (Annual Report 2024/25, Chairman's Statement). It earns money through tonnage produced x price per unit, with roughly two-thirds of revenue domestic and one-third export in FY2025 (Annual Report 2024/25, p.5). It is a subsidiary of PGP Glass Private Limited (India), which holds 78.65% of its equity -- a genuinely different legal entity from its Sri Lankan listed operating company, and this summary deliberately excludes the Indian parent's own financials, which are much larger and would misrepresent the Sri Lankan business if blended in. Revenue grew from LKR 8.5Bn (FY2021) to LKR 19.5Bn (FY2025), with profit after tax nearly quadrupling over the same period on margin expansion, not just volume (Ten Year Financial Review, Annual Report 2024/25, p.78). The single biggest recent dependency: fiscal policy (SSCL and Advance Personal Income Tax) has been directly compressing the domestic beverages segment's demand for glass packaging (Annual Report 2024/25, Chairman's Statement).
summary.gaps_note: Two documents originally backfilled for FY2022 and FY2023 turned out to be PGP Glass Private Limited's (the Indian parent) own annual reports, not PGP Glass Ceylon PLC's -- they were removed from the document library after discovery. FY2021-FY2025 figures used here instead come from the Ten Year Financial Review table inside the correctly-sourced FY2024/25 Annual Report, which is the company's own audited historical summary, not a re-derivation.

thesis.thesis_text: PGP Glass Ceylon is a capital-intensive glass-container manufacturer with the strongest balance sheet in this pilot set: FY2025 debt/equity is effectively zero (0.003x), current ratio 4.26x, and ROE 32.2%. Profit grew 41.4% YoY on 9.6% revenue growth, indicating real margin expansion, and the 4.05% dividend yield with a balanced 53.7% payout suggests management is comfortable returning cash while still funding growth. Note this annual report is denominated in absolute Rs, not Rs'000, and several negative-figure cells suffered a PDF font-encoding glitch; cost of sales and tax expense were reconstructed from clean anchor subtotals and cross-checked digit-by-digit, while capex was left blank rather than guessed (Annual Report FY2025, p.32-33).
thesis.gaps_note: Macro & Industry Outlook (10% weight) unavailable -- no CBSL/IMF/World Bank/news data source exists in this project; the remaining five pillars are renormalized to sum to 100% (Financial Quality 33.3%, Growth 22.2%, Valuation 22.2%, Business Quality 16.7%, Governance & Risk 5.6%). Governance & Risk is also necessarily thin -- no circulars/disclosures feed exists (deliberately disabled this session), so insider transactions, board changes, and rights issues cannot be verified directly; the score below reflects only what's visible in audited financial statements and public market data.

financial_quality.rationale: FY2025 ROE 32.2%, ROA 25.4%, net margin 21.3% -- exceptionally strong for an industrial manufacturer. Current ratio 4.26x and debt/equity effectively 0.003x (near debt-free) is a standout balance sheet among the pilot set.

growth_outlook.rationale: Revenue +9.6% YoY (17.8bn to 19.5bn), PAT +41.4% YoY (2.94bn to 4.16bn) -- profit growing far faster than revenue, a genuine margin-expansion story, not just top-line growth.

valuation.rationale: P/E 13.2x, P/B 4.26x (premium justified by 32% ROE), dividend yield 4.05% with a balanced 53.7% payout -- reasonably priced for the growth and quality on offer, with a genuinely attractive yield.

business_quality.rationale: Niche B2B glass container manufacturer (bottles/jars) serving beverage, cosmetics, and pharma customers with growing US export exposure -- diversified end markets and a capital-intensive manufacturing moat (real barrier to entry).

governance_risk.rationale: Near-debt-free balance sheet and clean, consistent reporting; no disclosures feed to verify board/ownership changes independently.

key_reasons: Near debt-free (debt/equity 0.003x) with ROE of 32.2% -- rare combination of low risk and high returns
PAT growth of 41.4% far outpaced revenue growth of 9.6% -- genuine margin expansion
4.05% dividend yield is the highest among the pilot set with a sustainable 53.7% payout
watch_factors: PDF font-encoding corruption affected several negative figures in the source filing -- capex was left blank rather than reconstructed; a future filing should confirm the pattern
Only 2 periods of financials on file -- can't yet confirm whether FY2025's margin jump is a durable trend or a one-off
Export/US exposure noted in the summary but not quantified here -- a demand-side risk not directly measurable from these financials

horizon_notes.6m: Watch for the FY2026 interim to confirm the FY2025 margin-expansion trend continues.
horizon_notes.1y: If ROE and margins hold near current levels, 13.2x P/E with a 4% yield looks attractive versus the balance-sheet quality on offer.
horizon_notes.3y: Case depends on sustained export growth (US, per company summary) and continued capital discipline given the near-zero debt load.
horizon_notes.5y: No 5-year data on file to verify a longer-run trend; would need additional annual reports backfilled to assess.

interim_updates.note_text: PGP Glass Ceylon posted Rs.5.10bn revenue for Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), roughly flat QoQ (-0.4% vs Q4 FY2025/26's Rs.5.12bn) and up 10.8% YoY. The story is entirely in the margin: gross margin jumped from 25.7% (Q4) to 36.0% (Q1) as cost of sales fell from 74.3% to 64.1% of revenue, driving operating profit up 44% QoQ (Rs.998mn to Rs.1.44bn) and PAT up 37% QoQ (Rs.860mn to Rs.1.17bn) on essentially flat revenue. Finance costs rose sharply both QoQ (Rs.11mn to Rs.53mn) and YoY (Rs.1mn to Rs.53mn), consistent with the Rs.2.5bn long-term borrowing drawn down during Q4 FY2025/26 (per that quarter's cash flow statement) now accruing a first full quarter of interest. YoY, PAT grew 19.0% (Rs.987mn to Rs.1.17bn) on a similar gross-margin improvement (33.0% to 36.0%).
interim_updates.gaps_note: PGP Glass's interim filings contain no chairperson's message or MD&A section -- only the four primary statements and brief notes -- so the cause of the gross-margin swing (input costs, mix, FX) cannot be confirmed from the filing itself; only the effect is quantifiable. The Q4 FY2025/26 filing (source_id 51275) discloses cash flow for the full year only, not the quarter in isolation, so QoQ cash-flow metrics are not available above.
interim_updates.takeaway: Both QoQ and YoY trends are genuinely positive -- revenue is stable to growing while gross margin expanded sharply, more than offsetting a new interest cost from Q4's Rs.2.5bn long-term borrowing. Unlike JKH or CCS, PGP Glass's interim filings are bare financial statements with no chairperson's commentary, so the specific cause of the margin improvement (input costs, product mix, FX on imported raw materials) cannot be confirmed from this filing alone.
operational_highlights: Revenue Rs.5.10bn, roughly flat QoQ (-0.4%) and up 10.8% YoY
Gross margin expanded sharply: 25.7% (Q4 FY2025/26) to 36.0% (Q1 FY2026/27), the main driver of a 44% QoQ rise in operating profit
PAT Rs.1.17bn, up 37% QoQ and 19% YoY
Finance costs rose to Rs.53mn (from Rs.11mn in Q4, Rs.0.7mn a year earlier), consistent with a Rs.2.5bn long-term loan drawn down in Q4 FY2025/26 now accruing a full quarter of interest
Net cash used in investing activities Rs.500mn, mostly a Rs.615mn increase in PPE purchases vs Rs.13mn a year earlier
key_drivers: QoQ, the entire profit improvement is a gross-margin story: cost of sales fell from 74.3% to 64.1% of revenue while revenue was flat, not a volume or pricing effect

Finance costs increased roughly 5x QoQ (Rs.11mn to Rs.53mn) -- the balance sheet shows non-current interest-bearing borrowings of Rs.1.43bn as at 31 March 2026 (zero a year earlier) following a Rs.2.5bn long-term loan drawdown recorded in the Q4 FY2025/26 cash flow statement
YoY, gross margin also improved (33.0% to 36.0%), suggesting the QoQ margin gain is not purely a one-quarter anomaly, though only two data points are on file so far
